lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p19 - Listen, point and say

details: Listen, Point and Say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows they match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds, and confident repetition.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

details: Point and match gives students controlled practice identifying the target language and showing their understanding of the questions What pet is this? and Where’s the…?
Look for correct matching of the pets in the picture dictionary strips to the pets in the main scene and accurate pointing to the pets shown.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p65 - Point and say: What’s missing?

details: Point and say provides controlled practice in recognising the target language and producing early-stage pronunciation. It also supports recall as students identify the missing pet.
Look for correct identification of the missing pet, accurate pointing, and correct pronunciation of the target language.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p19 - Say the chant and point to the pets

details: Say the chant and point to the pets strengthens retention of the target language (names of pets) and helps improve pronunciation and stress.
Look for correct stress, confident participation, with most students able to join in with at least the most repeated parts of the chant and some of the TPR actions.
